newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine ex-general indicted for comments on Jews.
newsitem.headline: Argentine ex-general indicted for comments on Jews.

text.p: A former Argentine army general once jailed for "Dirty War" human rights crimes was indicted on Wednesday on charges of encouraging racial hatred by making anti-Semitic comments to a magazine.

Court sources said Federal Judge Claudio Bonadio decided to try Carlos Suarez Mason for telling Argentina's top-selling weekly news magazine Noticias in a recent interview: "I am not anti-Semitic but I know the Jews and I don't trust them."

Suarez Mason was jailed for 43 murders and 24 kidnaps committed in the military's brutal 1976-83 rule, but was freed under an amnesty for "Dirty War" officers granted by the President Carlos Menem when he came to power in 1989.
In the interview, he denied the military juntas used torture but said that if they had done, they should have legalised it.

"Maybe we should have legalised it to cover some excesses, like the Jews do, beating a few people to death a day...but they had the audacity to make it law. Of course, the Jews have world power, so no one criticises them," he said in the interview, without elaborating.

The judge accepted for hearing a suit filed against Suarez Mason by Argentina's Jewish community, one of the world's largest, under local anti-racism laws which outlaw declarations "that incite violence and racial hatred."
